name: M5-FactoredSlot + adaptive threshold (default segmenter)

training.corpus: phase1 anchor 10,069 train / 529 val docs (2,788,159 sents)
training.anchor_labels: S5 v3.1 frozen prompt, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B no-thinking, k=1

signal: s = sum_k P(reset_k)  (5-axis reset probability sum)

threshold.formula: boundary if s_t >= running_mean(s_<t) + c * running_std(s_<t)   (adaptive, online)
threshold.provenance: c=1.0 was selected on the SuperDialseg official test (36,109 transitions): best adaptive rule on tiage (+0.071) and dialseg711 (+0.042). dev-3 argued AGAINST it (adaptive 0.3862 < fixed 0.3987) -- so this is NOT selection-on-dev.
threshold.why_not_fixed_quantile: r=0.0642 scored higher on dev-3 (0.4191 vs 0.3617) but its provenance is void: r was the anchor boundary rate under `count >= t*=3`, and t*=3 was discarded (D-B33 amendment 1) as a leftover operating point from before any threshold rule existed. Keeping a number whose definition was retired is circular.
threshold.known_cost: over-segments ~2.4x on dev-3 (160 predicted vs 66 gold). Boundary-count control is the open problem (D-B37/38).
superseded: fixed_quantile r=0.0642 (D-B30; provenance void after t*=3 was discarded)
otsu (parameter-free but scores at/below the no-boundary floor: 0.2831 vs 0.2790)

caveats: threshold frozen on the anchor corpus (D-B29), NOT on dev-3 -- dev-3 was never used for selection
trained on English narrative fiction only (D-M8); dialogue / Korean / non-narrative are out of domain
anchor label self-agreement S_self = 0.659 -- an upper bound on achievable performance
SEM inheritance is representational only; sticky-CRP + likelihood-ratio + local MAP were implemented, tested, and rejected (D-B28)

reference_scores.note: deployable pooled DTS Score on dev-3 (3 documents, 3 seeds). dev-3 is a practice set with 9 rounds of accumulated selection pressure on pieman -- quote deltas and direction, never the absolute number as performance.
reference_scores.reading: The adopted rule is NOT the highest-scoring one on dev-3. It is the highest-scoring one whose parameter has a provenance outside the evaluation set and outside the discarded t*=3 definition, and it is the only online (no-lookahead) rule -- required by RQ2. oracle_count_matched (0.4519) shows the ranking is already good and the loss is in count calibration, not in ranking.
